newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WMC says gold hedge increase was strategic.
newsitem.headline: WMC says gold hedge increase was strategic.

text.p: Australian mining group WMC Ltd said on Wednesday its gold hedging strategy was set in May 1996 after a review of its worldwide gold operations.
Chris Leptos, WMC's general manager of corporate development said the company had then changed its hedging strategy.

"One of the key findings coming out of that strategy was that we needed to adopt a position that we called discipline hedging and that for a proportion of our production we ceased to take a view on the gold price - we just hedge it as a matter of course within certain parameters," he said.
The strategy was linked to the gold price curve and results in WMC now hedging between 20 percent to 60 percent of its gold production on a continuous basis, Leptos said.

"By November (1996) we had in place a strategy that said we would hedge more, we would hedge on a disciplined basis and we would hedge on ten years of production rather than five years of production," he said.
WMC's gold hedge book rose to 3.04 million ounces as at June 30 from 727,000 ounces at the end of September 1996, its latest quarterly report, issued on Wednesday, shows.
Leptos said another factor contributing to the large increase in WMC's gold hedge book was the planned A$157 million expansion of its St Ives gold mine in Western Australia.

"At the time we made the announcement (to expand St Ives) we went into the hedge market and took out a hedge position there in excess of one million ounces of gold to cover the return on the capital component of the expansion," Leptos said.
WMC announced on Wednesday that it had deferred the expansion due to the fall in the price of gold.
Leptos had been asked about Australian press comment that WMC's hedging programme had thrown into question the role of the independent board members of the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA).
WMC managing director Hugh Morgan is a member of the central bank's board.
The RBA's announcement on July 4 that it had sold 167 tonnes of its reserves over a period of six months sent the price of gold tumbling to a 12 year low.
Leptos said Morgan would be making no comment.
